title: Savings Meltdown Recovery Board
oneLiner: A household emergency recovery workspace that helps users stop a cash-burn spiral after a bad month and choose the least-damaging sequence of cuts, negotiations, and bridge moves.
targetUser: Households or solo adults who have just taken a financial hit from job loss, debt shock, medical expense, or failed side income and need a rapid stabilization plan.
keyUX: See exactly where the cash burn is happening, compare rescue options, and walk away with a 14-day stabilization sequence instead of frozen panic.
stitchPrompt: Design a desktop emergency household finance workspace called Savings Meltdown Recovery Board for people facing sudden cash-burn panic after a bad month. It should help users understand where the money bleed is happening, compare cut-delay-negotiate options, evaluate bridge cash sources, and build a 14-day stabilization sequence before fear causes worse decisions. Include a cash-burn emergency summary, a bill triage priority queue, a cut-delay-negotiate simulator, a bridge-cash option matrix, a 14-day stabilization board, and a don’t-make-it-worse warning drawer. Design direction: use an operator-dense aesthetic with deep charcoal and navy structure, compact actionable modules, one hard alert accent, and survival-first hierarchy so the product feels serious, protective, and decisively useful.
